series: Things Living In Your House, Part 40
sources: Mayo Clinic, Dust mite allergy, diagnosis and treatment: wash sheets, blankets, pillowcases and bedcovers in hot water at least 130 F (54.4 C) to kill dust mites and remove allergens, or dry them at least 20 minutes above 130 F; freezing items for 24 hours kills mites but doesn't remove allergens; https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/dust-mites/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20352178

National Jewish Health, Dust Mite Allergy: wash all bedding weekly in hot (130 F) water; inhaled droppings or skin contact may cause allergy, asthma and/or eczema symptoms; https://www.nationaljewish.org/conditions/allergy/overview/allergens/dust-mite

title: Your Bed Mites Die at 130°F 😬 (Things Living In Your House #40)

beats.say: Wash your sheets under 130 degrees, and the mites in your bed live.
They crawl back into your pillow. And eat your skin.
Their poop can set off asthma and eczema.
Can't wash it? Freeze it for 24 hours. They die.
But the poop stays behind. So go hot, because
